title: CHM301: Organic Chemistry and Hydrocarbons (170 Questions)

questions.prompt: What is organic chemistry mainly the study of?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon and its compounds.

questions.prompt: Which elements are found in a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds, but not every organic compound is a hydrocarbon.

questions.prompt: Which substance is a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: C2H4 contains only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which substance is NOT a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethanol contains oxygen, so it is organic but not a hydrocarbon.

questions.prompt: Why is carbon able to form many compounds?
questions.explanation: Carbon has four valence electrons and can form four bonds.

questions.prompt: How many bonds can carbon normally form to achieve a stable octet?
questions.explanation: Carbon normally forms four bonds.

questions.prompt: Which is a property of organic compounds?
choices: They are always soluble in water.
questions.explanation: Organic compounds are generally nonelectrolytes.

questions.prompt: Why do many organic compounds react slowly?
questions.explanation: Many organic compounds react slowly because they are covalent.

questions.prompt: Which statement about melting and boiling points is generally correct?
questions.explanation: Organic compounds usually have low melting and boiling points.

questions.prompt: Which statement about organic compounds and water is correct?
choices: They are usually soluble and miscible.
They are usually insoluble and immiscible.
They are always ionic in water.
questions.explanation: Organic compounds are usually insoluble and immiscible in water.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an organic compound?
questions.explanation: Methanol is an organic compound.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethene contains only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only hydrocarbons?
questions.explanation: Both propane and butane contain only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only organic compounds but not necessarily hydrocarbons?
questions.explanation: Glucose and benzene are organic compounds; glucose contains oxygen.

questions.prompt: What does a molecular formula show?
choices: The number of atoms of each element
questions.explanation: A molecular formula shows the number of atoms of each element.

questions.prompt: What is the molecular formula of propane?
questions.explanation: Propane is C3H8.

questions.prompt: Which type of formula shows the arrangement of atoms?
questions.explanation: A structural formula shows atom arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which formula is the most informative?
questions.explanation: A structural formula shows both atoms and their arrangement.

questions.prompt: What is the condensed formula of propane?
questions.explanation: The condensed formula of propane is CH3CH2CH3.

questions.prompt: What does a condensed formula combine?
questions.explanation: A condensed formula combines structural and molecular information.

questions.prompt: What is a homologous series?
choices: A sequence of organic compounds with similar characteristics
questions.explanation: It is a sequence with the same general formula and similar chemical properties.

questions.prompt: Members of a homologous series usually differ by:
questions.explanation: Successive members usually differ by one CH2 unit.

questions.prompt: Why do members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties?
choices: They contain the same functional group.
They have exactly the same formula.
questions.explanation: Similar chemical properties result from the same functional group.

questions.prompt: Which property gradually changes as molecular mass increases?
questions.explanation: Physical properties such as boiling point gradually change.

questions.prompt: Which belongs to the alkane homologous series?
questions.explanation: Methane is an alkane.

questions.prompt: What is the general formula for alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow CnH2n+2.

questions.prompt: Which type of bond exists between carbon atoms in alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes contain C-C single bonds.

questions.prompt: Alkanes are described as:
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons.

questions.prompt: What does saturated mean for an alkane?
choices: It contains the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: Saturated alkanes have the maximum number of hydrogens.

questions.prompt: Which is the first member of the alkane series?
questions.explanation: Methane is first.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is in the correct order?
questions.explanation: This is the correct alkane order.

questions.prompt: Which formula represents methane?
questions.explanation: Methane is CH4.

questions.prompt: Which formula represents ethane?
questions.explanation: Ethane is C2H6.

questions.prompt: Which formula represents butane?
questions.explanation: Butane is C4H10.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between CH4 and C2H6?
questions.explanation: Successive alkanes differ by CH2.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between C2H6 and C3H8?
questions.explanation: Each successive alkane differs by CH2.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a homologous series is FALSE?
choices: Members have the same general formula.
Every member has exactly the same molecular formula.
questions.explanation: Members have different molecular formulas.

questions.prompt: Which formula is a molecular formula?
questions.explanation: C3H8 gives the number of each atom.

questions.prompt: Which formula is a condensed formula?
questions.explanation: CH3CH2CH3 is condensed propane.

questions.prompt: Which statement about molecular formulas is correct?
choices: They show the exact arrangement of atoms.
They show the number of each type of atom.
questions.explanation: Molecular formulas show atom counts.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives more information about atom arrangement?
questions.explanation: Structural formulas show arrangement.

questions.prompt: A compound contains only carbon and hydrogen. What can it be classified as?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: A compound contains C, H, and O. Can it be a hydrocarbon?
choices: Yes, if it has more carbon
Only if it is a gas
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Benzene contains only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Which compound contains oxygen and therefore is not a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Phenol contains oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which change would you expect across a homologous series as molecular mass increases?
questions.explanation: Boiling point, melting point, and density can change gradually.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why members of a homologous series react similarly?
choices: They have the same molecular mass.
They contain the same functional group.
They all contain the same number of atoms.
They all have the same physical properties.
questions.explanation: The same functional group gives similar chemical properties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT an alkane?
questions.explanation: For three carbons, an alkane is C3H8.

questions.prompt: Which statement summarizes the alkane series correctly?
choices: Alkanes contain C=C bonds and follow CnH2n.
Alkanes contain C-C single bonds and follow CnH2n+2.
Alkanes contain C triple bond C and follow CnH2n-2.
Alkanes contain oxygen and follow CnH2n+2.
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with C-C single bonds and CnH2n+2.

questions.explanation: A bond represents two shared electrons.

questions.explanation: An alkane with nine carbons is nonane.

questions.explanation: C5H12 follows CnH2n+2.

An alkane has 15 carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?

questions.explanation: 2n + 2 = 22 gives n = 10.

Which pair represents consecutive alkane members?
questions.explanation: Consecutive members differ by CH2.

questions.explanation: C2H6 + CH2 = C3H8.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃?
questions.explanation: It has four carbon atoms and only single bonds.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₂=CH₂?
questions.explanation: It has two carbon atoms and one double bond.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for HC≡CH?
questions.explanation: It has two carbon atoms and one triple bond.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₂=CH—CH₃?
questions.explanation: The structure has three carbon atoms and a double bond beginning at carbon 1.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₃—CH=CH—CH₃?
questions.explanation: The double bond starts at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for HC≡C—CH₂—CH₃?
questions.explanation: The four-carbon chain has a triple bond beginning at carbon 1.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₂=CH—CH₂—CH₃?
questions.explanation: It has four carbon atoms and a double bond beginning at carbon 1.

questions.prompt: Which structure represents but-2-ene?
questions.explanation: The double bond is between carbon 2 and carbon 3.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon has five carbon atoms and only single bonds. What is its name?
questions.explanation: Five carbons give pent-, and single bonds give -ane.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon has six carbon atoms and one double bond. Which family does it belong to?
questions.explanation: A carbon–carbon double bond identifies an alkene.

questions.prompt: A straight-chain hydrocarbon has eight carbon atoms and one triple bond. What prefix should be used?
questions.explanation: Oct- represents eight carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for a straight-chain hydrocarbon with nine carbon atoms and only single bonds?
questions.explanation: Nine carbons give non-, and single bonds give -ane.

questions.prompt: Which name represents a ten-carbon alkane?
questions.explanation: Dec- represents ten carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: A student names a four-carbon molecule containing a triple bond as butene. What is the mistake?
choices: The number of carbon atoms is incorrect.
questions.explanation: A triple bond requires the suffix -yne, not -ene.

questions.prompt: Why is the position number important in naming some alkenes?
choices: The double bond can occur in different positions.
All double bonds are always at carbon 1.
questions.explanation: Different positions of a double bond can produce different structures.

questions.prompt: Which name is correctly written for a four-carbon alkene with its double bond starting at carbon 1?
questions.explanation: But- represents four carbons, 1 indicates the bond position, and -ene identifies the double bond.

questions.prompt: What does the number in but-2-ene represent?
choices: The position where the double bond starts
questions.explanation: The number 2 indicates that the double bond starts at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: Which naming sequence is correct?
choices: Identify bond → count carbons → choose prefix → name
Count longest chain → choose prefix → identify bond → number if needed → name
Count hydrogen atoms → identify oxygen → name
Find molecular mass → choose suffix → name
questions.explanation: These are the main steps for naming simple hydrocarbons.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of a three-carbon hydrocarbon containing a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Prop- represents three carbon atoms and -yne represents a triple bond.

questions.prompt: What is a branched hydrocarbon?
choices: A hydrocarbon with no carbon atoms
A hydrocarbon with a carbon chain containing side groups
A hydrocarbon with only triple bonds
questions.explanation: Branched hydrocarbons have carbon groups attached to the parent chain.

questions.prompt: What should you identify first when naming a branched alkane?
questions.explanation: The longest chain determines the parent name.

questions.prompt: What is the name of a one-carbon branch?
questions.explanation: A CH₃ branch is called methyl.

questions.prompt: What is the name of a two-carbon branch?
questions.explanation: A two-carbon branch is called ethyl.

questions.prompt: From which end should a branched alkane be numbered?
choices: The end nearest the first branch
questions.explanation: This gives the branch the lowest possible position number.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃—CH(CH₃)—CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has three carbon atoms, with a methyl branch on carbon 2.

questions.prompt: What is the parent chain in 2-methylbutane?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous chain contains four carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: In 2-methylbutane, what does the number 2 indicate?
choices: The methyl branch is attached to carbon 2
questions.explanation: The number indicates the position of the branch.

questions.prompt: Which structure represents 2-methylbutane?
questions.explanation: It contains a four-carbon parent chain with a methyl branch at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix di- mean in a chemical name?
questions.explanation: Di- indicates two identical substituent groups.

questions.prompt: What does tri- indicate in a branched hydrocarbon name?
questions.explanation: Tri- means three identical substituent groups.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of a butane chain with methyl branches on carbons 2 and 3?
questions.explanation: There are two methyl branches attached to carbons 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: What does dimethyl indicate?
questions.explanation: Di- means two, and methyl identifies the branch.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for a five-carbon parent chain with a methyl branch at carbon 3?
questions.explanation: Five parent-chain carbons give pentane, and the methyl branch is on carbon 3.

questions.prompt: Why identify the longest continuous chain in a branched hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: The parent name comes from the longest continuous carbon chain.

questions.prompt: Which rule is used when numbering a branched alkane?
choices: Give the branch the highest number
Give the first branch the lowest possible number
questions.explanation: Numbering begins from the end nearest the first branch.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon has two identical methyl branches. Which prefix should be used?
questions.explanation: Two identical branches are represented using di-.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name for CH₃—CH(CH₃)—CH₂—CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons, and the methyl branch is at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: A student numbers a branched chain from the wrong end and gets branch number 3 instead of 2. What should they do?
choices: Number from the opposite end to obtain the lower number
Change the parent chain to methane
questions.explanation: The lowest possible branch position should be used.

questions.prompt: If numbering from either end gives the same set of locants, which numbering should be chosen?
choices: Lowest number at the first point of difference
questions.explanation: Choose the lowest number at the first point of difference.

questions.prompt: A company processes crude oil to produce gasoline. Which area of chemistry is mainly involved?
questions.explanation: Gasoline contains hydrocarbons studied in organic chemistry.

questions.prompt: Which is a real-life use of hydrocarbons?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are important components of vehicle fuels.

questions.prompt: Which industry uses organic compounds to manufacture plastics?
questions.explanation: The petrochemical industry uses petroleum-derived compounds to manufacture plastics.

questions.prompt: Why are hydrocarbons important in the energy industry?
questions.explanation: Many hydrocarbons release energy during combustion.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes organic compounds and hydrocarbons?
choices: All hydrocarbons are organic compounds, but not all organic compounds are hydrocarbons.
questions.explanation: Organic compounds can contain elements other than carbon and hydrogen.

questions.prompt: C₆H₁₂ is assumed to be a simple open-chain hydrocarbon with one double bond. Which family?
questions.explanation: It follows the alkene formula CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon contains seven carbon atoms and follows the alkane formula. What is its formula?
questions.explanation: Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, n = 7 gives C₇H₁₆.

questions.prompt: A compound has five carbon atoms and belongs to the alkyne family. What is its formula?
questions.explanation: Using CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, n = 5 gives C₅H₈.

questions.prompt: What do methane, ethane, propane and butane have in common?
choices: They belong to the alkane homologous series
questions.explanation: All four are alkanes and follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a homologous series?
choices: Same general formula, similar chemical properties and successive members differing by CH₂
questions.explanation: These are the main characteristics of a homologous series.

questions.prompt: What is the correct IUPAC name of CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 5 carbon atoms and the methyl branch is at carbon 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 4 carbon atoms and two methyl branches are attached to carbon 2.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct IUPAC name: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 5 carbons with methyl branches at 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of a pentane chain with ethyl and methyl branches both on carbon 3?
questions.explanation: Both branches are attached to carbon 3; ethyl is written before methyl alphabetically.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 6 carbons; numbering from the left gives branch 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 6 carbons, with ethyl at 4 and methyl at 2.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name: CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 6 carbons and methyl branches are at 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–C(CH₃)₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 5 carbons with methyl branches at 2, 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain contains 6 carbons and the ethyl branch is at carbon 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: Numbering from the left gives methyl branches at 2, 4 and 4.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₂=C(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The double bond starts at carbon 1 and the methyl branch is at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name of CH₃–C(CH₃)=CH–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The double bond is at carbon 2 and the methyl branch is also at carbon 2.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₂=CH–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: Numbering starts at the double bond, placing it at 1 and the methyl at 3.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name of CH₃–CH=CH–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: Numbering gives the double bond position 2 and the methyl branch position 4.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of HC≡C–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The triple bond starts at carbon 1 and the methyl branch is at carbon 3.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name of CH₃–C≡C–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The triple bond starts at carbon 2 and the methyl branch is at carbon 4.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of CH₂=CH–CH₂–C≡CH?
questions.explanation: Both numbering directions give 1,4; the double bond receives the lower number.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name of CH₂=C(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The double bond starts at 1, with methyl branches at 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: What is the correct name of HC≡C–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃?
questions.explanation: The triple bond starts at carbon 1 and the methyl branch is at carbon 4.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH=CH–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.explanation: The double bond is at carbon 3 from either direction; the branch receives position 2.
